## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Not justified. E2-E11 do not cleanly separate the proposed top call from the runner-up: tubulin and actin rise together, cell rounding/mitotic arrest rises monotonically, and the 30 uM well has only 114 cells with extreme z-scores, so bright tubulin could be confinement in mitotic cells rather than specific bundle formation. The e4 description reports intact/brighter tubulin and bright rounded mitotics, not clear bundle morphology in interphase cells. Most importantly, both atlas queries return zero neighbors for the proposed top class while repeatedly returning the runner-up and other classes (e5/e11: e.g. 0/10 and 0/10 for the top class despite the proposed call), which makes 0.62 appear overconfident. A cleaner discriminator is available without a new acquisition: run a reference-atlas comparison on the already acquired low-toxicity 1 uM well, where tubulin is elevated but the mitotic fraction is essentially baseline. If the proposed mechanism is correct, that well should move toward the correct neighborhood; if it still clusters with mitotic-kinesin/actin/protein-synthesis references, the top call should fall.

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Protein synthesis**, BBBC021 annotates **Epithelial**.

## Reflection

The dose-dependent signal was real but nonspecific: tub_mean rose monotonically (e8 rho=+1.00) with frac_mitotic_like rise (e9) and cell loss (e10), and high doses showed very large tubulin and actin texture z-scores (e3 tub_mean +11.9, e6 tub_glcm_contrast +43.8 and act_glcm_contrast +77.8). The review was right that this did not separate stabilizer from runner-ups, because actin rose together with tubulin, the 30 uM well had only 114 cells, and e4 reported intact/brighter tubulin with bright rounded mitotics rather than clear interphase bundles.
The discriminator acquisition behaved as requested but misled the revision: compare_to_reference_atlas on the low-toxicity 1 uM well (e14) gave 0/10 stabilizer and 5/10 protein synthesis, following e5 and e11 which also gave 0/10 stabilizer while repeatedly returning protein synthesis, actin disruptors and Eg5 inhibitors. I demoted stabilizer 0.62 to 0.15 and promoted protein synthesis to 0.35 on atlas-count logic alone, without testing confinement artifact or mimicry.
Unblinded truth was Epithelial, so both calls were wrong. With no structure from lookup_compound (e17, AZ-U internal code), I had no chemical prior and over-trusted an atlas that did not represent the true class; persistent anisomycin-like similarity (PMID 3401749) and stabilizer-like mitotic arrest (PMID 14522931, PMID 20442307) were morphological mimics of rounding, condensation and toxicity rather than mechanism proof.

What was right:
- Flagged dose-dependent cytoskeletal condensation with mitotic-like arrest and cell loss as the dominant phenotype across e2, e3, e6, e8, e9 and e10.
- Recognized from e5, e11 and e14 that the atlas never supported stabilizer (0/10, 0/10, 0/10) and that 0.62 was overconfident given intact-filament description in e4.
- Applied the requested 1 uM low-mitotic discriminator and correctly lowered the stabilizer hypothesis after it still clustered away from stabilizers.

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted monotonic tub_mean rise (e8) as stabilizer-specific while ignoring parallel act_glcm_contrast elevation (+9.8 to +77.8 in e2, e3, e6), which favored general condensation/rounding in mitotics over specific bundle formation.
- Overweighted extreme z-scores from the 30 uM well with only 114 cells (e6), where confinement in rounded cells inflates tubulin/actin intensity and texture.
- Overcorrected to protein synthesis 0.35 on e14 5/10 counts alone without ruling out that translation-inhibitor neighbors are condensation mimics, and missed that the true Epithelial class was not discriminated by the chosen tubulin/mitotic/cell-count acquisition set.

Proposed next experiment: Repeat 1 and 10 uM with high-resolution confocal for alpha-tubulin plus E-cadherin/keratin/vimentin, F-actin and pH3 with single-cell interphase vs mitotic gating and cell-number-matched controls, plus puromycin-incorporation SUnSET vs cycloheximide/anisomycin and washout viability, and compare directly to epithelial-reference compounds to test adhesion/differentiation versus translation inhibition.

- PMID [3401749](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3401749/): Anisomycin, an inhibitor of protein synthesis, blocks late phases of LTP phenomena in the hippocampal CA1 region in vitro. *Brain Res* (1988) — Anisomycin is a protein synthesis inhibitor, relevant to the protein-synthesis atlas neighbors that drove the revised call.
